subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core `sleep` self-pause tool, and if so should it be implemented as a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted tool with explicit sandbox policy?
rationale: The request adds model-facing core scheduling behavior and crosses session-state, gateway cron, interruption, restart, and sandbox boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent API and security semantics.

options.title: Sponsor corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the capability but require the implementation to resume the originating session, cancel or preempt on user input, enforce a hard cap, lose timers on restart, and keep sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep current cron/session guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and continue routing delayed work through cron, process completion wakes, and `sessions_yield` for subagent completion only.

options.title: Narrow to extension API design
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension seam if maintainers want optional sleep behavior outside the default core tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the capability but require the implementation to resume the originating session, cancel or preempt on user input, enforce a hard cap, lose timers on restart, and keep sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans agent runtime, cron/session scheduling, and sandbox policy, and this is the strongest current routing signal from recent area history and prior ClawSweeper review context.
